explanation: This slide compares population dynamics between More-Developed Countries (MDCs) and Less-Developed Countries (LDCs). 1) MDCs (including North America, Europe, Japan, and Australia) feature slow population growth and a high standard of living. These nations have undergone a demographic transition—characterized by a decrease in death rates followed by a decrease in birth rates—stabilizing their population growth. 2) LDCs (including Latin America, Africa, and Asia) display rapid population growth and a low standard of living. Strategies to reduce population growth in LDCs include family planning programs, social progress (which can lower the desire for larger families), and delaying the onset of childbearing.

questions.q: What is a demographic transition as described in the notes?
opts: An increase in birth rates followed by an increase in death rates
A decrease in death rates followed by a decrease in birth rates
The migration of populations from LDCs to MDCs
The transition from agriculture to high technology in LDCs
questions.exp: The notes define a demographic transition as 'decreased death rate followed by decreased birth rate' which has occurred in MDCs.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed as a strategy to reduce population growth in Less-Developed Countries (LDCs)?
opts: Social progress to reduce the desire for large families
questions.exp: The notes list three strategies to reduce population growth: 'Family planning programs', 'Social progress, which may reduce the desire for large families', and 'Delay the onset of childbearing.' 'Forced urbanization' is not mentioned.
